rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The soul is ruined when God buries it in disobedience.
rows.anchor: أي خسرت نفس دسها الله عز وجل بالمعصية

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās explains it as a soul God led astray and caused to deviate.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن عباس : خابت نفس أضلها وأغواها

rows.speaker: قتادة وغيره
rows.claim: Qatāda and others contrast the successful person who purifies the soul through obedience and good works with one who buries it in sins.
rows.anchor: وقيل : أفلح من زكى نفسه بطاعة الله ، وصالح الأعمال ، وخاب من دس نفسه في المعاصي . قاله قتادة وغيره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Zakāh fundamentally means growth and increase; the crop grows abundantly, and a judge's validation and praise elevate a witness.
rows.anchor: وأصل الزكاة : النمو والزيادة ، ومنه زكا الزرع : إذا كثر ريعه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The one who does good and hastens to righteous works makes himself known and raises himself, like generous Arabs who camp high and light fires for travelers.
rows.anchor: فمصطنع المعروف والمبادر إلى أعمال البر ، شهر نفسه ورفعها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Miserly Arabs hid in caves, outskirts, and valley bottoms; morally, they concealed and buried themselves, unlike those who elevate and purify themselves.
rows.anchor: فأولئك علوا أنفسهم وزكوها ، وهؤلاء أخفوا أنفسهم ودسوها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A sinner is characteristically obscure and low in standing, with head bowed because of committing sins.
rows.anchor: وكذا الفاجر أبدا خفي المكان ، زمر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An unattributed interpretation glosses d s y as leading astray; the cited poem uses it of luring and ruining ʿAmr.
rows.anchor: وقيل : دساها : أغواها . قال :

rows.speaker: أهل اللغة
rows.claim: Linguists derive the form from dassasah, concealment, with the second s changed to y as in qaṣṣaytu from qaṣaṣtu; taqaḍḍu likewise becomes taqaḍḍī.
rows.anchor: قال أهل اللغة : والأصل : دسسها ، من التدسيس ، وهو إخفاء الشيء

rows.speaker: ابن الأعرابي
rows.claim: Ibn al-Aʿrābī says it means hiding oneself among the righteous while not actually belonging to them.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن الأعرابي : " وقد خاب من دساها " أي دس نفسه في جملة الصالحين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The address means: I warned you and made you fear the punishment.
rows.anchor: فأنذرتكم " أي حذرتكم وخوفتكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The fire blazes and burns; the form is originally tatalaẓẓā.
rows.anchor: أي تلهب وتتوقد وأصله تتلظى

rows.speaker: عبيد بن عمير ويحيى بن يعمر وطلحة بن مصرف
rows.claim: ʿUbayd ibn ʿUmayr, Yaḥyā ibn Yaʿmar, and Ṭalḥah ibn Muṣarrif read the fuller form تتلظى.
rows.anchor: وهي قراءة عبيد بن عمير ، ويحيى بن يعمر ، وطلحة بن مصرف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He gives without seeking repayment for anyone's favor; he seeks his transcendent Lord's good pleasure, and will be satisfied by the recompense.
rows.anchor: أي ليس يتصدق ليجازي على نعمة ، إنما يبتغي وجه ربه الأعلى ، أي المتعالي

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: ʿAṭāʾ and al-Ḍaḥḥāk report from Ibn ʿAbbās that persecuted Bilāl cried One, One; the Prophet promised God would save him and alerted Abū Bakr, who bought and freed him, prompting the charge that Abū Bakr repaid a favor and this verse's revelation.
rows.anchor: فروى عطاء والضحاك عن ابن عباس قال : عذب المشركون بلالا ، وبلال يقول أحد أحد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another account says Abū Bakr bought Bilāl from Umayya and Ubayy ibn Khalaf for a cloak and ten uqiyyas and freed him for God; it associates the revelation with 92:4.
rows.anchor: وقيل : اشترى أبو بكر من أمية وأبي بن خلف بلالا ، ببردة وعشر أواق ، فأعتقه لله

rows.speaker: سعيد بن المسيب
rows.claim: Saʿīd ibn al-Musayyib reports that Umayya offered Bilāl for Nustās, Abū Bakr's wealthy polytheist slave; Abū Bakr offered to make Nustās Muslim and transfer his property, but he refused, so Abū Bakr exchanged him for Bilāl, leading the polytheists to allege a debt to Bilāl.
rows.anchor: وقال سعيد بن المسيب : بلغني أن أمية بن خلف قال لأبي بكر حين قال له أبو بكر : أتبيعنيه ؟

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The exception is disconnected, meaning but seeking God's face, so it is accusative; he illustrates this with no one in the house except a donkey, while nominative is also possible.
rows.anchor: فهو استثناء منقطع ؛ فلذلك نصبت . كقولك : ما في الدار أحد إلا حمارا . ويجوز الرفع

rows.speaker: يحيى بن وثاب
rows.claim: Yaḥyā ibn Waththāb reads ابتغاء in the nominative, reflecting the dialect that permits a nominative after إلا; poetry and 4:66 illustrate this usage.
rows.anchor: وقرأ يحيى بن وثاب " إلا ابتغاء وجه ربه " بالرفع ، على لغة من يقول : يجوز الرفع في المستثنى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Face of the Lord means His approval and what draws one near Him; al-Aʿlā describes the Lord, who possesses the attributes of exaltedness.
rows.anchor: من نعت الرب الذي استحق صفات العلو

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: By the sense of the sentence, seeking the Lord's face can be a purpose complement: he gives wealth only to seek God's face, not to repay a favor.
rows.anchor: مفعولا له على المعنى ؛ لأن معنى الكلام : لا يؤتي ماله إلا ابتغاء وجه ربه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He will receive in Paradise what pleases him, with a reward many times greater than what he spent.
rows.anchor: أي سوف يعطيه في الجنة ما يرضي ، وذلك أنه يعطيه أضعاف ما أنفق

rows.speaker: علي
rows.claim: Abū Ḥayyān al-Taymī transmits from his father, from ʿAlī, the Prophet's prayer for Abū Bakr, who married him to his daughter, carried him to the migration home, and freed Bilāl from his wealth.
rows.anchor: وروى أبو حيان التيمي عن أبيه عن علي رضي الله عنه ، قال : قال رسول الله

rows.speaker: بلال
rows.claim: When Abū Bakr bought him, Bilāl asked whether he had been bought for service or for God's cause; Abū Bakr said God's cause, and freed him.
rows.anchor: ولما اشتراه أبو بكر قال له بلال : هل اشتريتني لعملك أو لعمل الله

rows.speaker: عمر بن الخطاب
rows.claim: ʿUmar called Abū Bakr their master and Bilāl the master whom Abū Bakr freed.
rows.anchor: وكان عمر بن الخطاب رضي الله عنه يقول : أبو بكر سيدنا وأعتق سيدنا يعني بلالا

rows.speaker: عطاء وابن عباس
rows.claim: ʿAṭāʾ, with a report from Ibn ʿAbbās, says the sūra came down about Abū al-Daḥdāḥ and the palm he bought with his orchard; al-Qushayrī says Ibn ʿAbbās specified forty palms but did not name the man.
rows.anchor: وقال عطاء - وروى عن ابن عباس - : إن السورة نزلت في أبي الدحداح ، في النخلة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An Anṣārī's palm dropped dates into a neighbor's home, where children took them; after the Prophet's offer of a palm in Paradise was refused, Abū al-Daḥdāḥ traded his orchard for it and gave the palm to the neighbor, and the sūra was revealed about them.
rows.anchor: كان لرجل من الأنصار نخلة ، يسقط من بلحها في دار جار له ، فيتناول صبيانه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In the Abū al-Daḥdāḥ story, the giver is Abū al-Daḥdāḥ, al-ḥusnā is the reward, and the easy way is Paradise.
rows.anchor: يعني أبا الدحداح .   " وصدق بالحسنى "  أي بالثواب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In this account, the miser is the Anṣārī, al-ḥusnā is the reward, and the hard way is Hell.
rows.anchor: يعني الأنصاري .   " وكذب بالحسنى "  أي بالثواب .   " فسنيسره للعسرى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The miser's wealth cannot help at death; the one who enters the fire is the hypocritical Khazrajī, who died in hypocrisy, while Abū al-Daḥdāḥ is kept from it.
rows.anchor: أي مات . إلى قوله : " لا يصلاها إلا الأشقى " يعني بذلك الخزرجي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The one spending to purify himself is Abū al-Daḥdāḥ paying for the palm; he owed nobody a favor to repay, and acted only for God's sake.
rows.anchor: يكافئه عليها ، يعني أبا الدحداح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This verse answers the preceding oath.
rows.anchor: قوله تعالى : " ما ودعك ربك " هذا جواب القسم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When Gabriel was delayed, the polytheists said God had abandoned and hated the Prophet, so the verse was revealed.
rows.anchor: وكان جبريل عليه السلام أبطأ على النبي صلى اللّه عليه وسلم ، فقال المشركون : قلاه اللّه وودعه ، فنزلت الآية

rows.speaker: ابن جريج
rows.claim: Ibn Jurayj says revelation was withheld from the Prophet for twelve days.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن جريج : احتبس عنه الوحي اثني عشر يوما

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās gives the hiatus as fifteen days.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن عباس : خمسة عشر يوما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An unnamed report gives a twenty-five-day hiatus in revelation.
rows.anchor: وقيل : خمسة وعشرين يوما

rows.speaker: مقاتل
rows.claim: Muqātil says the hiatus lasted forty days.
rows.anchor: وقال مقاتل : أربعين يوما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The polytheists argued that if Muhammad's mission came from God, revelation would continue for him as it had for earlier prophets.
rows.anchor: ولو كان أمره من اللّه لتابع عليه ، كما كان يفعل بمن كان قبله من الأنبياء

rows.speaker: جندب بن سفيان
rows.claim: Al-Bukhārī reports from Jundub ibn Sufyān that the Prophet was ill and did not rise for two or three nights; a woman said his demon had left him, and the verses were revealed.
rows.anchor: وفي البخاري عن جندب بن سفيان قال : اشتكى رسول اللّه صلى اللّه عليه وسلم ، فلم يقم ليلتين أو ثلاثا

rows.speaker: جندب البجلي
rows.claim: Al-Tirmidhī reports Jundub al-Bajalī's account of the Prophet's wounded, bleeding finger and Gabriel's delay, after which the polytheists said he had been abandoned; the verse came down.
rows.anchor: وفي الترمذي عن جندب البجلي قال : كنت مع النبي صلى اللّه عليه وسلم في غار فدميت إصبعه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Tirmidhī grades the report sound and fair; he omits the two-or-three-night detail found in al-Bukhārī, which Qurtubī calls the soundest account.
rows.anchor: هذا حديث حسن صحيح . لم يذكر الترمذي : " فلم يقم ليلتين أو ثلاثا " أسقطه الترمذي .

rows.speaker: جندب بن سفيان البجلي
rows.claim: Al-Thaʿlabī also reports Jundub ibn Sufyān al-Bajalī: a stone struck the Prophet's finger, he bled and stayed up from night prayer for two or three nights, then Umm Jamīl taunted him and the sūra descended.
rows.anchor: وقد ذكره الثعلبي أيضا عن جندب بن سفيان البجلي ، قال : رمي النبي صلى اللّه عليه وسلم في إصبعه بحجر

rows.speaker: أبو عمران الجوني
rows.claim: Abū ʿImrān al-Jawnī says Gabriel's delay distressed the Prophet, who prayed with his forehead against the Kaʿba; Gabriel tapped his shoulders and the verse was revealed.
rows.anchor: وروى عن أبي عمران الجوني قال : أبطأ جبريل على النبي صلى اللّه عليه وسلم حتى شق عليه

rows.speaker: خولة
rows.claim: Khawla found a dead puppy under the bed after days without revelation; when she removed it, Gabriel arrived, the Prophet trembled and asked to be covered, and Gabriel explained angels do not enter a house with a dog or image.
rows.anchor: وقالت خولة - وكانت تخدم النبي صلى اللّه عليه وسلم - : إن جروا دخل البيت ، فدخل تحت السرير فمات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another account links the hiatus to questions from Jews about the spirit, Dhū al-Qarnayn, and the Companions of the Cave: the Prophet promised a reply tomorrow without saying if God wills, so 18:23 arrived and Gabriel answered them.
rows.anchor: وقيل : لما سألته اليهود عن الروح وذي القرنين وأصحاب الكهف قال : [ سأخبركم غدا ]

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A report says Muslims asked why revelation stopped; the Prophet attributed the delay to their failure to clean finger joints, trim nails, and shorten moustaches, then Gabriel explained he was a commanded servant and cited 19:64.
rows.anchor: وقيل : إن المسلمين قالوا : يا رسول اللّه ، مالك لا ينزل عليك الوحي ؟

rows.speaker: ابن عباس وابن الزبير
rows.claim: The majority read the verb with doubling, from tawdīʿ, like bidding farewell; Ibn ʿAbbās and Ibn al-Zubayr are reported to read it lightly, meaning left you.
rows.anchor: ودعك " بالتشديد : قراءة العامة ، من التوديع ، وذلك كتوديع المفارق . وروي عن ابن عباس وابن الزبير أنهما قرآه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A cited poem uses wadaʿnā to mean we left; al-Mubarrad says wadaʿa and wadhara are rarely used because initial wāw is weak, and speakers use taraka instead.
rows.anchor: وثم وَدَعنا آلَ عمرو وعامر

rows.speaker: محمد بن يزيد المبرد
rows.claim: Al-Mubarrad explains that forms beginning with weak wāw were largely replaced by the verb meaning leave.
rows.anchor: قال المبرد محمد بن يزيد : لا يكادون يقولون ودع ولا وذر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase means the Lord has not hated the Prophet after loving him; the object pronoun is omitted because this is an end of a verse.
rows.anchor: قوله تعالى : " وما قلى " أي ما أبغضك ربك منذ أحبك . وترك الكاف ، لأنه رأس آية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qilāʾ means hatred; with fatḥa on qāf the word is lengthened, with forms like qalāhu yaqlīhi, and Ṭayyiʾ uses yaqlāhu.
rows.anchor: والقلى : البغض ، فإن فتحت القاف مددت ، تقول : قلاه يقليه قلى وقلاء .

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Thaʿlab's cited verse is glossed as we do not hate her, confirming that q-l-y means hatred.
rows.anchor: أي لا نبغضها .   ونقلي أي نبغض

rows.speaker: امرؤ القيس
rows.claim: Imruʾ al-Qays's phrase maqlī witnesses the sense of being hated.
rows.anchor: وقال امرؤ القيس : ولستُ بمَقْلِيِّ الخِلالِ ولا قال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The full sense is that the Lord has neither left nor hated the Prophet; the object pronoun is likewise omitted at the verse ending in 33:35, where the meaning supplies remembrance of God.
rows.anchor: وتأويل الآية : ما ودعك ربك وما قلاك . فترك الكاف لأنه رأس آية ، كما قال عز وجل

rows.speaker: ابن إسحاق
rows.claim: Ibn Isḥāq says what awaits Muhammad in his return to God is better than the worldly honor granted him quickly.
rows.anchor: روى سلمة عن ابن إسحاق قال : " وللآخرة خير لك من الأولى " أي ما عندي في مرجعك إلي يا محمد

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says the Prophet was shown what God would open for his community after him and rejoiced; Gabriel then brought these promises.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن عباس : أري النبي صلى اللّه عليه وسلم ما يفتح اللّه على أمته بعده ؛ فسر بذلك ؛ فنزل جبريل بقوله

rows.speaker: ابن إسحاق
rows.claim: Ibn Isḥāq glosses the promise as victory in this world and reward in the next.
rows.anchor: قال ابن إسحاق : الفلج في الدنيا ، والثواب في الآخرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An alternative explanation is the Pool and intercession.
rows.anchor: وقيل : الحوض والشفاعة

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: A report from Ibn ʿAbbās, raised by al-Awzāʿī, says the Prophet was shown his community's future and received a thousand musk-soil pearl palaces in Paradise, with suitable spouses and servants in each.
rows.anchor: وعن ابن عباس : ألف قصر من لؤلؤ أبيض ترابه المسك . رفعه الأوزاعي

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says Muhammad's satisfaction meant that no member of his household would enter Hell; al-Suddī is also named at this point.
rows.anchor: وعنه قال : رضي محمد ألا يدخل أحد من أهل بيته النار . وقال السدي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another view takes the promise as intercession for all believers.
rows.anchor: وقيل : هي الشفاعة في جميع المؤمنين

rows.speaker: علي
rows.claim: ʿAlī reports the Prophet saying God will grant him intercession for his community until God asks if he is pleased, and he answers that he is.
rows.anchor: وعن علي رضي الله عنه قال : قال رسول الله صلى اللّه عليه وسلم : ( يشفعني الله في أمتي حتى يقول الله سبحانه لي : رضيت يا محمد

rows.speaker: عبدالله بن عمرو بن العاص
rows.claim: In Muslim, ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAmr reports the Prophet reciting Abraham 14:36 and Jesus 5:118, praying and weeping for his community; God tells Gabriel to reassure him that He will satisfy him concerning his community and not grieve him.
rows.anchor: وفي صحيح مسلم عن ، عبدالله بن عمرو بن العاص أن النبي صلى اللّه عليه وسلم تلا قول اللّه تعالى في إبراهيم

rows.speaker: علي
rows.claim: ʿAlī tells the Iraqis that although they regard 39:53 as the most hopeful verse, the Prophet's family regards this promise as the most hopeful.
rows.anchor: وقال علي رضي الله عنه لأهل العراق : إنكم تقولون إن أرجى آية في كتاب الله تعالى : " قل يا عبادي الذين أسرفوا

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: A hadith says that when this verse came down, the Prophet swore he would not be satisfied while one member of his community remained in the Fire.
rows.anchor: وفي الحديث : لما نزلت هذه الآية قال النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم : [ إذاً والله لا أرضى وواحد من أمتي في النار

rows.speaker: ابن إسحاق
rows.claim: Ibn Isḥāq says what awaits Muhammad in his return to God is better than the worldly honor granted him quickly.
rows.anchor: روى سلمة عن ابن إسحاق قال : " وللآخرة خير لك من الأولى " أي ما عندي في مرجعك إلي يا محمد

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: A hadith says that when this verse came down, the Prophet swore he would not be satisfied while one member of his community remained in the Fire.
rows.anchor: وفي الحديث : لما نزلت هذه الآية قال النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم : [ إذاً والله لا أرضى وواحد من أمتي في النار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase means that God lifted the Prophet's sin from him.
rows.anchor: قوله تعالى : " ووضعنا عنك وزرك " أي حططنا عنك ذنبك

rows.speaker: أنس
rows.claim: Anas is reported to read the phrase with the alternatives wa-ḥallalnā and wa-ḥaṭaṭnā.
rows.anchor: وقرأ أنس " وحللنا ، وحططنا " .

rows.speaker: ابن مسعود
rows.claim: Ibn Masʿūd reads: We removed from you your burden.
rows.anchor: وقرأ ابن مسعود : " وحللنا عنك وقرك " .

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse parallels the forgiveness promised in 48:2.
rows.anchor: هذه الآية مثل قوله تعالى : " ليغفر لك الله ما تقدم من ذنبك وما تأخر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One view places all of this before prophethood; al-Qurṭubī explains the burden as the Prophet's pre-Islamic ways shared with his people, although he never worshipped an idol or image.
rows.anchor: قيل : الجميع كان قبل النبوة . والوزر : الذنب ، أي وضعنا عنك ما كنت فيه من أمر الجاهلية

rows.speaker: قتادة والحسن والضحاك
rows.claim: Qatāda, al-Ḥasan, and al-Ḍaḥḥāk say the Prophet had sins weighing on him, which God forgave.
rows.anchor: قال قتادة والحسن والضحاك : كانت للنبي صلى اللّه عليه وسلم ذنوب أثقلته ، فغفرها اللّه له

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The burden made his back so heavy that its creaking could be heard; Arabic usage also describes a load creaking on a camel and a saddle creaking.
rows.anchor: أي أثقله حتى سمع نقيضه ، أي صوته . وأهل اللغة يقولون : أنقض الحمل ظهر الناقة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jamīl's poem uses naqīḍ for the ropes' creaking and describes the front supports of the chest as nearly breaking.
rows.anchor: قال جميل : وحتى تداعت بالنَّقِيضِ حبالُه

rows.speaker: المحاسبي
rows.claim: Al-Muḥāsibī says the burden would have weighed on him had God not pardoned him.
rows.anchor: قال المحاسبي : يعني ثقل الوزر لو لم يعف اللّه عنه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The burden made the Prophet's back heavy and weakened it.
rows.anchor: أي أثقله وأوهنه . قال : وإنما وصفت ذنوب الأنبياء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Prophets' sins are described as burdensome despite forgiveness because they are deeply concerned by them, regret them, and grieve over them.
rows.anchor: وإنما وصفت ذنوب الأنبياء بهذا الثقل ، مع كونها مغفورة ، لشدة اهتمامهم بها

rows.speaker: السدي
rows.claim: Al-Suddī explains removing the burden as lifting the Prophet's weight.
rows.anchor: وقال السدي : " ووضعنا عنك وزرك " أي وحططنا عنك ثقلك

rows.speaker: عبد الله بن مسعود
rows.claim: A reading attributed to ʿAbd Allāh ibn Masʿūd says: We lifted your burden from you.
rows.anchor: وهي في قراءة عبد الله بن مسعود " وحططنا عنك وقرك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some explain the burden as the weight of pre-Islamic sins.
rows.anchor: وقيل : أي حططنا عنك ثقل آثام الجاهلية

rows.speaker: الحسين بن المفضل
rows.claim: Al-Ḥusayn ibn al-Mufaḍḍal takes it to mean error and inadvertence.
rows.anchor: قال الحسين بن المفضل : يعني الخطأ والسهو

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some say the burden is the sins of the Prophet's community, attributed to him because his heart was occupied with them.
rows.anchor: وقيل : ذنوب أمتك ، أضافها إليه لاشتغال قلبه بها

rows.speaker: عبد العزيز بن يحيى وأبو عبيدة
rows.claim: ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz ibn Yaḥyā and Abū ʿUbayda say God lightened the burdens of prophethood and carrying it so it would not weigh on him.
rows.anchor: وقال عبد العزيز بن يحيى وأبو عبيدة : خففنا عنك أعباء النبوة والقيام بها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One account says revelation initially weighed on the Prophet until he nearly threw himself from a mountain; Gabriel showed himself and relieved his fear that his reason had changed.
rows.anchor: وقيل : كان في الابتداء يثقل عليه الوحي ، حتى كاد يرمي نفسه من شاهق الجبل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another view says God protected him from bearing sin and kept him free of impurities through the forty years before revelation, which came to him purified.
rows.anchor: وقيل : عصمناك عن احتمال الوزر ، وحفظناك قبل النبوة في الأربعين من الأدناس

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujāhid explains the raising of the Prophet's mention as its inclusion in the call to prayer.
rows.anchor: قال مجاهد : يعني بالتأذين

rows.speaker: حسان بن ثابت
rows.claim: Ḥassān ibn Thābit's poem says God marked the Prophet with prophethood and joined his name to God's in the muezzin's testimony of faith in the five prayers.
rows.anchor: وضم الإله اسمَ النبي إلى اسمه

rows.speaker: الضحاك عن ابن عباس
rows.claim: Al-Ḍaḥḥāk reports Ibn ʿAbbās: whenever God is mentioned, Muhammad is named with Him in prayer, festivals, pilgrimage rites, marriage sermons, and across the world.
rows.anchor: وروي عن الضحاك عن ابن عباس ، قال : يقول له لا ذُكِرتُ إلا ذُكِرتَ معي

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says a person who worships God and affirms the afterlife without bearing witness that Muhammad is God's messenger gains nothing and is an unbeliever.
rows.anchor: ولو أن رجلا عبد اللّه جل ثناؤه ، وصدق بالجنة والنار وكل شيء ، ولم يشهد أن محمدا رسول اللّه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another view says God elevated his mention in earlier revealed books, commanded earlier prophets to announce him, and will make his religion prevail over every religion.
rows.anchor: وقيل : أي أعلينا ذكرك ، فذكرناك في الكتب المنزلة على الأنبياء قبلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Other views place his elevated mention among the angels in heaven and believers on earth, and in the Hereafter through the Praiseworthy Station and noble ranks.
rows.anchor: وقيل : رفعنا ذكرك عند الملائكة في السماء ، وفي الأرض عند المؤمنين
